title: PRIMA-Plus: Development and piloting of a brief psychological intervention by general practitioners for the treatment of PTSD symptoms in women after traumatic childbirth
summary:
The birth of a child is a profound life event that can be associated with significant psychological stress for many women. In some cases, this can lead to serious conditions such as depression, anxiety disorders or post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Approximately 3 to 6% of all women meet the clinical criteria for PTSD after giving birth. Those affected often suffer from unwanted flashbacks of the trauma in the form of distressing images, emotional numbness and increased nervousness and tension. In addition, many try to avoid memories or situations related to childbirth. Such symptoms are mainly caused by extreme stress during childbirth, such as severe pain, medical emergencies, complications or the frightening feeling of total loss of control, for example during unplanned surgical procedures. 

Early treatment is essential in order to prevent long-term negative consequences for the mother's mental and physical health and for the child's development. In Germany, however, care provision faces major challenges. There is a significant shortage of available psychotherapy places, meaning that waiting times of over three months are common. Furthermore, as there is no uniformly regulated care structure for women with postpartum stress, there is often a gap in care. General practitioners must therefore play a key role in long-term care in order to identify affected women at an early stage and offer them a reliable point of contact.  

Narrative exposure therapy is a low-threshold psychotherapeutic approach to treating symptoms of PTSD that can be offered by individuals without basic psychotherapeutic training. The core of the method is the structured narrative processing of stressful life experiences along a chronological timeline, whereby traumatic experiences are remembered in detail, verbalised and integrated into the autobiographical context (exposure). The aim is to process the traumatic memories emotionally and reduce PTSD symptoms. The intervention was developed and successfully tested in the PICTURE study for patients after a stay in intensive care. In the PRIMA-Plus pilot study, it has now been adapted to the specific patient group by integrating a birth protocol. The intervention is designed to help patients process symptoms of PTSD after a traumatic birth and prevent the development of subsequent mental health conditions. The aim of this intervention is not to replace psychotherapeutic or psychiatric care. Rather, it can help alleviate mild to moderate symptoms or bridge the waiting period for a therapy place.

Research question: 
The aim of this study is to investigate the feasibility, i.e. relevance, acceptance and practicability of adapted narrative exposure therapy in women with symptoms of PTSD following traumatic birth experiences in primary care, and to identify factors that promote and hinder the further implementation of the intervention. Secondary endpoints of this pilot study are changes in symptoms of PTSD, depression and anxiety disorder, the parent-child relationship and the quality of life of the patients.

Methods:
The PRIMA-Plus study is a pilot study. Its purpose is to examine whether the intervention appears feasible in normal everyday practice. We are accompanying a group of 40 women in total, with the aim of recruiting around two to three patients for the project in each participating GP practice. This number of participants was deliberately chosen so that we can obtain reliable scientific results while ensuring that the study remains feasible in normal everyday practice.

Women who are at least 18 years old, have a very good command of German and have given birth to a child in a hospital in the past 12 months are eligible to participate in the study. An important part of the preparation is that we request a birth report from the respective maternity clinic in order to carry out the psychological counselling. In addition, it is a prerequisite that the women concerned suffer from mild to moderate stress symptoms, which we determine in advance using a special questionnaire to assess stressful experiences. However, certain reasons mean that participation in this special study is not possible. This applies to women who have already been in therapeutic or psychiatric treatment for mental health issues within the last year or who are currently suffering from very severe symptoms of stress disorder or severe depression. Exclusion is also necessary in cases of acute suicidal thoughts, the use of certain high-dose medications for mental illness, or severe diagnoses such as postpartum schizophrenia. In these cases, intensive specialist care is required that goes beyond the scope of this short intervention by a general practitioner.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Traumatic birth experience in the 12 months prior to the start of the study
• Live birth in a hospital with an existing birth record
• PTSD-like symptoms with a Posttraumatic Diagnostic Scale for DSM-5 total score ≥15 and <70 points
• Ability to comply with study procedures
• Sufficient knowledge of the German language
• Written consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Psychiatric and psychotherapeutic care during the last 12 months, existing or planned participation in trauma-focused psychotherapy at the start of the study
• Severe symptoms of PTSD (PDS-5 > 70)
• Acute suicidality 
• Taking high-dose antidepressant/antipsychotic/ anticholinergic medication
• Inability to give informed consent 
• Severe physical or psychiatric illness
